explication:
## Purpose and runtime
kube-state-metrics is a Go service that reads Kubernetes API object state and exposes derived Prometheus-format metrics. It does not persist or forward metrics; its in-memory view reflects currently existing cluster objects. The executable starts at `main.go`, with application/server wiring in `pkg/app/server.go`. It is deployed as a container (`Dockerfile`) or Kubernetes workload (`examples/standard/deployment.yaml`).

## Process entry, configuration, and composition
Startup parses CLI configuration, Kubernetes connection settings, resource/namespace selection, metric allow/deny filters, sharding, and optional custom-resource definitions. Options feed construction of the application’s API clients, registries, stores, watchers, and HTTP servers.
- `main.go`
- `pkg/options/options.go`
- `pkg/app/server.go`

## Kubernetes discovery and watch boundary
The service’s external state source is the Kubernetes API server, accessed through `client-go`. Discovery resolves supported API resources and their versions before informer/list-watch setup. Informers continuously list and watch selected objects, retaining local cache state; API availability and RBAC permissions are therefore key operational boundaries.
- `internal/discovery/discovery.go`
- `internal/discovery/types.go`
- `pkg/watch/watch.go`

## Resource stores and metric generation
Per-resource stores transform cached Kubernetes objects into metric families. The builder assembles enabled stores for core, apps, RBAC, networking, storage, policy, and other supported APIs. Individual resource implementations encode the metric schema and translate raw object fields/labels into Prometheus-safe output.
- `internal/store/builder.go`
- `internal/store/pod.go`
- `internal/store/deployment.go`

## Metric model, registry, and scrape-time assembly
Generated metric families are held in a metrics store and written on demand. The metric generator applies configured metric filters; the HTTP metrics handler can further select/exclude resource groups per request. This separates continuous Kubernetes cache updates from scrape-time Prometheus serialization.
- `pkg/metric/family.go`
- `pkg/metrics_store/metrics_store.go`
- `pkg/metric_generator/generator.go`
- `pkg/metricshandler/metrics_handler.go`

## HTTP exposure and observability
The main exposition server provides plaintext `/metrics` (default port 8080), plus main-server health endpoints. A separate telemetry server (default 8081) exposes process/build/configuration, HTTP, and Kubernetes list/watch result metrics, with readiness on that boundary.
- `pkg/app/server.go`
- `pkg/metricshandler/metrics_handler.go`
- `pkg/watch/watch.go`

## Scale, filtering, and extension paths
Horizontal sharding assigns objects by UID hash, while node-oriented pod handling constrains list/watch scope; all shards may still receive API traffic. Resource selection and label/metric allow-deny behavior limit generated output. Custom Resource State configuration creates dynamic metrics for CRDs; this extension is feature-frozen in favor of resource-state-metrics.
- `pkg/sharding/listwatch.go`
- `pkg/allowdenylist/allowdenylist.go`
- `pkg/customresourcestate/registry_factory.go`
- `pkg/customresource/registry_factory.go`
